assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators turned band topology into a organising principle for real materials: the Z2 invariant, protected edge and surface states and the quantum spin Hall effect are clean, general mechanisms that reshaped condensed-matter physics and spawned a large field. This is the kind of simple, universal idea I value, and it is understood, not merely observed.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theory (quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 classification in graphene-based models); Molenkamp's group made the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. Other theorists (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Balents and others) and ARPES experimenters have strong claims, and those names are not in the credited list, so the three-person configuration is defensible but leaves unresolved credit.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed over about 15 years across many materials (HgTe, Bi-based compounds, ARPES, transport). Interpretation stable. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether Kane-Mele plus Molenkamp is the right trio given theory credit for HgTe and 3D topological insulators spread across several people.
I am recalling the history from memory and have not verified the detailed priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock (magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms) gave a step change in frequency metrology, reaching fractional uncertainties around 1e-18 and enabling tests of relativity, searches for new physics and relativistic geodesy. Originality is clear, impact is broad and the idea is conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and demonstrated early versions; Ye led the development to record accuracy and the many-body control, with Hall and Hansch already recognised in 2005 for the comb. A two-person award looks clean; others (Lemonde, Takamoto, Kimble, Ludlow, Hinkley) contributed but are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple groups worldwide operate such clocks, the redefinition of the SI second is being discussed, and results are reproduced at the 1e-18 level. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Possible overlap in the committee's mind with the 2005 prize and with ion clocks (Wineland 2012), which may affect perceived novelty.
Exact priority among Katori, Ye and others for the lattice-clock concept is only partly known to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture identifies a critical-like transition in disordered, athermal matter with universal scaling of contacts and elastic moduli and a link between rigidity, soft modes and the vibrational density of states. It is a compact mechanism that unifies grains, foams, emulsions and glasses and is exactly the sort of universality that connects complex systems to a clean model.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram (1998) and drove the subsequent theory and experiment programme; credit for the isostatic-point scaling and marginal stability is shared with O'Hern, Silbert, Wyart, Mezard, Parisi and others who are not in the list. A two-person award is natural but not the only possible allocation.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of simulation, theory and experiments; the mean-field theory of jamming in infinite dimensions strengthens the picture. Some debate remains about how far the jamming critical point controls real finite-temperature glasses.
uncertainties: The extent to which jamming explains experimental systems rather than idealised ones is debated.
Credit relative to the later theory (marginal stability, replica mean field) is unresolved.
Impact on technology is indirect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation defines a universality class for non-equilibrium interface growth with exact solutions connecting to random-matrix statistics (Tracy-Widom), and Takeuchi's liquid-crystal experiments confirmed the predicted distributions. It is a rare case of exact theory, universal scaling and clean experiment meeting. As someone working with random matrices and stochastic processes, I find this very compelling.
assessment.attribution: The 1986 Kardar-Parisi-Zhang paper is foundational, but Giorgio Parisi is already a laureate (2021) and is not among the credited names; exact solutions (Johansson, Prahofer-Spohn, Sasamoto-Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel) and Takeuchi's experiments are separate contributions. A prize for the theory plus experiment is possible, but the attribution is genuinely awkward.
assessment.maturity: The experimental confirmation (2010-2011) has been replicated in other systems, and the mathematical side is well developed. Interpretation is stable; recognition would not be premature.
uncertainties: Whether the exact-solution mathematicians deserve recognition alongside the physicists.
Parisi's absence from the credited list complicates a fair trio.
Experimental scope is limited to a few systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek model and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory established that flocks can show long-range order in two dimensions, with anomalous fluctuations and universal exponents; it created the field of active matter. The idea is a simple mechanism with a rigorous renormalisation-group analysis and strong cross-disciplinary reach (birds, bacteria, cytoskeleton, robots).
assessment.attribution: Vicsek introduced the minimal numerical model (1995); Toner and Tu gave the hydrodynamic theory and RG exponents (1995, 1998), with Toner's earlier work crucial. These three are a coherent configuration. Others (Ramaswamy, Marchetti, Cates) are important for active-matter theory broadly but are not in the credit list.
assessment.maturity: Theory is well established; direct quantitative experimental confirmation of the Toner-Tu exponents is limited, with some support from simulations and a few experiments on colloids and vibrated granular matter. Recognition might be slightly early but the conceptual impact is mature.
uncertainties: Weak quantitative experimental validation of the exact exponents.
Whether the committee would treat active matter as a mature topic yet.
Priority issues relative to Ramaswamy and Marchetti's work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory in two dimensions gave exact critical exponents, classification of universality classes and tools used across statistical mechanics, string theory and quantum field theory. It is among the most conceptually influential results in theoretical physics, though I note Polyakov's own broad portfolio overlaps with the holography candidate.
assessment.attribution: The 1984 BPZ paper was the decisive work, with the three credited names as authors; the Virasoro algebra, minimal models and Friedan-Qiu-Shenker unitarity work also mattered, and Friedan, Cardy, and Fateev are not credited. The trio is neat but contested.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, over 40 years, with confirmation from exact solutions, numerics and experiments on 2D critical systems (Ising, Potts). Recognition is late rather than early, and some laureates have died.
uncertainties: Is the work experimentally decisive enough for the physics prize, or too mathematical?
Credit to Cardy, Friedan and others outside the list.
Polyakov's possible parallel candidacy elsewhere.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos (2013), followed by the identification of TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy and made a gigaton detector in Antarctic ice a reality. It is a major experimental achievement with clear originality.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the programme; Karle was a leading figure in the construction and analysis. A large collaboration and the AMANDA pioneers, as well as the earlier proposals of Markov, Reines and Learned, complicate attribution; the prize rule of three limits fair recognition.
assessment.maturity: Discovery is robust and independent confirmation comes from KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD, but the source-identification picture is still developing, which makes some aspects premature.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration attribution under the three-person limit.
The astrophysical origin of the diffuse flux is not settled.
Whether source results are mature enough.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays opens a new gravitational-wave band and probes supermassive black-hole binaries and perhaps new physics. The result is exciting, and the Hellings-Downs correlation gives a quite clean signature.
assessment.attribution: The 2023 results came from NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA, PPTA and CPTA, each with large collaborations; the founding contributions go back to Detweiler, Hellings-Downs, Foster-Backer and others. A three-person list drawn from the supplied names cannot represent this fairly, and I treat the list as a compromise.
assessment.maturity: The evidence is around 2 to 4 sigma per array and the source (SMBH binaries versus new physics) is unresolved; detection with full significance and individual-source identification are still ahead, so it is probably premature.
uncertainties: Evidence strength is not yet discovery-level in the strictest sense.
Interpretation of the amplitude and the spectrum is open.
Attribution among four collaborations and earlier pioneers is unresolved.
